CHAPTER 14 — अमृतस्य पन्थाः (AMRITASYA PANTHAH — THE PATH OF IMMORTALITY)

Introduction — अमृतस्य पन्थाः कः?

The title of this chapter joins two weighty Sanskrit words: अमृतम् (amritam) and पन्थाः (panthah). अमृतम् is formed from the negative prefix अ + मृतम् (from the root मृ, 'to die') — literally 'that which does not die', the deathless, the imperishable. पन्थाः means 'path' or 'way'. अमृतस्य पन्थाः is therefore 'the path of immortality' — the way, taught in the Upanishads, by which a human being rises above the fear of death. The Upanishads are the concluding, philosophical portions of the Vedas (hence called वेदान्त), and they are entirely in the public domain of humanity's oldest wisdom literature. Their central question is exactly the question of this chapter: everything we see — body, wealth, house, kingdom — perishes; is there anything that does NOT perish, and how may we reach it? Their answer: the आत्मा, the innermost Self, is नित्य (eternal), and it is reached not by wealth (वित्तम्) but by knowledge (विद्या). As the Kena and Isha Upanishads declare, विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते — 'by knowledge one attains immortality'.

What immortality means here (अमृतत्वस्य अर्थः)

Senior-secondary students should note carefully: the Upanishads do not promise that the body will live forever. The body is by nature अनित्य (impermanent); it is born and it dies. अमृतत्वम् (immortality) in the Upanishadic sense is the direct knowledge that one's true Self — the आत्मा — is unborn, undying and imperishable. One who knows this crosses beyond the fear of death: तमेव विदित्वा अति मृत्युम् एति — 'knowing Him alone, one crosses over death'. The chapter therefore contrasts two categories again and again: the नित्य (eternal — आत्मा, विद्या, सत्यम्) and the अनित्य (transient — वित्तम्, शरीरम्, भोगाः). The path of immortality is the deliberate turning from the second to the first.

मैत्रेयी-याज्ञवल्क्य-संवादः — The Dialogue of Maitreyi and Yajnavalkya (बृहदारण्यकोपनिषद्)

The heart of this chapter is the celebrated dialogue between the sage याज्ञवल्क्यः and his wife मैत्रेयी, found in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad. Below it is retold in simple Sanskrit prose with translation.

1. याज्ञवल्क्यः महर्षिः गृहस्थाश्रमं परित्यज्य संन्यासं ग्रहीतुम् ऐच्छत्। तस्य द्वे भार्ये आस्ताम् — मैत्रेयी कात्यायनी च। तयोः मैत्रेयी ब्रह्मवादिनी आसीत्।
   (The great sage Yajnavalkya wished to leave the householder's life and take up renunciation. He had two wives — Maitreyi and Katyayani. Of the two, Maitreyi was a brahmavadini — a woman devoted to the inquiry into Brahman.)

2. सः मैत्रेयीम् उवाच — 'मैत्रेयि! अहम् अस्मात् स्थानात् उद्यास्यन् अस्मि। एहि, तव कात्यायन्याः च कृते वित्तस्य विभागं करोमि' इति।
   (He said to Maitreyi: 'Maitreyi! I am about to go forth from this place. Come, let me make a division of my wealth for you and Katyayani.')

3. मैत्रेयी अपृच्छत् — 'भगवन्! यदि इयं सर्वा पृथिवी वित्तेन पूर्णा मम स्यात्, किं तेन अहम् अमृता स्याम्?' इति।
   (Maitreyi asked: 'Revered sir! If this whole earth, filled with wealth, were mine, would I become immortal by that?')

4. याज्ञवल्क्यः अवदत् — 'न इति। यथा उपकरणवतां जीवितं भवति, तथा एव तव जीवितं स्यात्। अमृतत्वस्य तु न आशा अस्ति वित्तेन (अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन)' इति।
   ('No,' said Yajnavalkya. 'Your life would only be like the life of people who have every comfort and means. But of immortality there is no hope through wealth.')

5. तदा मैत्रेयी अवदत् — 'येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्? यत् एव भगवान् वेद — अमृतत्वस्य साधनम् — तत् एव मे ब्रूहि' इति।
   (Then Maitreyi said the immortal words: 'What shall I do with that by which I cannot become immortal? Tell me only that which you, revered one, know — the means of immortality.')

6. याज्ञवल्क्यः प्रसन्नः अभवत् अवदत् च — 'प्रिया एव असि मे, प्रियं च भाषसे। आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यः मन्तव्यः निदिध्यासितव्यः। आत्मनः दर्शनेन एव इदं सर्वं विदितं भवति। न वित्तेन, न कर्मणा, किन्तु आत्मज्ञानेन एव अमृतत्वं लभ्यते' इति।
   (Yajnavalkya was pleased and said: 'Dear you are to me, and dear is what you speak. The Self, dear one, must be seen — must be heard about, reflected upon, and deeply meditated upon. When the Self is realized, all this becomes known. Not by wealth, not by ritual acts, but by knowledge of the Self alone is immortality attained.')

7. सः च अवदत् — 'आत्मनः तु कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति' इति — पतिः, पत्नी, पुत्राः, वित्तम् — सर्वं आत्मनः एव कृते प्रियं भवति।
   (And he taught: 'It is for the sake of the Self that everything becomes dear' — husband, wife, children, wealth — all are dear only for the sake of the Self, the one supreme reality within.)

शब्दार्थ (dialogue): उद्यास्यन् = about to go forth/renounce; वित्तम् = wealth; विभागः = division; पूर्णा = filled; अमृता = immortal (feminine); उपकरणवताम् = of those who possess means/comforts; आशा = hope; येन = by which; कुर्याम् = shall I do (विधिलिङ्); ब्रूहि = tell (लोट्); द्रष्टव्यः = must be seen; श्रोतव्यः = must be heard; मन्तव्यः = must be reflected upon; निदिध्यासितव्यः = must be deeply meditated upon; विदितम् = known.

संवादस्य सन्देशः (Message of the dialogue): Maitreyi's question — येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम् — is one of the most piercing questions in world literature. She does not reject wealth out of contempt; she simply measures it against the highest goal and finds it insufficient. Wealth can buy comfort (उपकरणम्), never deathlessness. Her discrimination (विवेकः) between the eternal and the transient, and her courage to choose the eternal, make her the model of the true seeker. Yajnavalkya's reply gives the actual path: आत्मा must be realized through a threefold discipline — श्रवणम् (hearing the truth from the teacher and the Upanishads), मननम् (reasoning upon it until doubt is removed), and निदिध्यासनम् (deep, sustained meditation) — culminating in दर्शनम् (direct realization).

अमृत-मन्त्राः — Five public-domain verses on the path of immortality

1) असतो मा सद्गमय । तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय । मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय ॥ (बृहदारण्यकोपनिषद्)
   शब्दार्थ: असतः = from the unreal; मा = me; सत् = to the real; गमय = lead; तमसः = from darkness; ज्योतिः = to light; मृत्योः = from death; अमृतम् = to immortality.
   अन्वयः: (हे प्रभो!) मा असतः सत् गमय। मा तमसः ज्योतिः गमय। मा मृत्योः अमृतं गमय।
   Translation: Lead me from the unreal to the real; lead me from darkness to light; lead me from death to immortality.
   Message: The three movements — unreal to real, darkness to light, death to deathlessness — are three descriptions of the single journey of आत्मविद्या.

2) शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः ... (श्वेताश्वतरोपनिषद्)
   शब्दार्थ: शृण्वन्तु = let (them) listen (लोट्); विश्वे = all; अमृतस्य = of the immortal; पुत्राः = sons/children.
   अन्वयः: विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः शृण्वन्तु।
   Translation: Listen, all ye children of the Immortal!
   Message: The Upanishad addresses every human being as अमृतस्य पुत्रः — a child of immortality. Deathlessness is our birthright, not the privilege of a few.

3) विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह । अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते ॥ (ईशोपनिषद्)
   शब्दार्थ: विद्याम् = knowledge (of the Self); अविद्याम् = knowledge of the world/action; यः = who; उभयम् = both; सह = together; वेद = knows; अविद्यया = by worldly knowledge/action; मृत्युं तीर्त्वा = having crossed death (mortal difficulties); विद्यया = by Self-knowledge; अमृतम् = immortality; अश्नुते = attains.
   अन्वयः: यः विद्यां च अविद्यां च — तत् उभयं सह वेद, (सः) अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्यया अमृतम् अश्नुते।
   Translation: One who knows both vidya and avidya together crosses death by avidya and attains immortality by vidya.
   Message: Worldly knowledge and skill (अविद्या) carry us across life's mortal needs; but only आत्मविद्या gives immortality. Both are to be honoured, each in its own place.

4) श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः । श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभिप्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते ॥ (कठोपनिषद्)
   शब्दार्थ: श्रेयः = the (ultimately) good; प्रेयः = the (immediately) pleasant; मनुष्यम् एतः = come to man; तौ = those two; सम्परीत्य = having examined well; विविनक्ति = discriminates; धीरः = the wise/steadfast one; अभि वृणीते = chooses; मन्दः = the dull one; योगक्षेमात् = for the sake of worldly gain and security.
   अन्वयः: श्रेयः च प्रेयः च मनुष्यम् एतः। धीरः तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति। धीरः हि प्रेयसः श्रेयः अभिवृणीते। मन्दः योगक्षेमात् प्रेयः वृणीते।
   Translation: Both the good and the pleasant come to a person. The wise one examines the two and separates them; the wise chooses the good over the pleasant, while the dull one, for the sake of worldly gain and comfort, chooses the pleasant.
   Message: Every day life offers us the श्रेयस्-प्रेयस् choice. Maitreyi chose श्रेयस्; the path of immortality is walked by such choices.

5) वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम् आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् । तमेव विदित्वाति मृत्युमेति नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय ॥ (श्वेताश्वतरोपनिषद्)
   शब्दार्थ: वेद = know; अहम् = I; एतम् = this; पुरुषं महान्तम् = great Purusha (Supreme Being); आदित्यवर्णम् = radiant like the sun; तमसः परस्तात् = beyond darkness; तम् एव विदित्वा = knowing Him alone; अति मृत्युम् एति = one crosses beyond death; न अन्यः पन्थाः = no other path; विद्यते = exists; अयनाय = for going (to liberation).
   अन्वयः: अहम् एतं महान्तं पुरुषम् आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् वेद। तम् एव विदित्वा (जनः) मृत्युम् अति एति। अयनाय अन्यः पन्थाः न विद्यते।
   Translation: I know this great Purusha, radiant like the sun, beyond all darkness. Only by knowing Him does one cross beyond death; there exists no other path for that journey.
   Message: This verse gives the chapter its title: knowledge of the Supreme Self is THE path — नान्यः पन्थाः — the path of immortality.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the text

(A) सन्धिः (with सन्धि-विच्छेद): 
  • नामृता = न + अमृता (दीर्घ-सन्धिः: अ + अ = आ). Likewise नाशास्ति = न + आशा + अस्ति; वेदाहम् = वेद + अहम्.
  • विद्ययाऽमृतम् = विद्यया + अमृतम् (आ + अ = आ; the अवग्रह ऽ marks the merged अ).
  • मृत्योर्मा = मृत्योः + मा (विसर्ग-सन्धिः: visarga becomes र् before a soft sound). Likewise तमसो मा = तमसः + मा and असतो मा = असतः + मा (visarga becomes ओ).
  • सद्गमय = सत् + गमय (व्यञ्जन-सन्धिः: त् becomes द् before the soft ग्). Likewise तद्वेद = तत् + वेद.
  • चाविद्याम् = च + अविद्याम् (दीर्घ-सन्धिः); श्रेयश्च = श्रेयः + च (visarga becomes श् before च).

(B) तव्यत्-प्रत्ययः (gerundive — 'must be / should be done'): the four famous words of Yajnavalkya's teaching are all तव्यत् forms: द्रष्टव्यः (दृश् + तव्यत् = must be seen), श्रोतव्यः (श्रु + तव्यत् = must be heard), मन्तव्यः (मन् + तव्यत् = must be reflected on), निदिध्यासितव्यः (नि + ध्यै, desiderative + तव्यत् = must be deeply meditated upon). The तव्यत् form expresses duty or necessity and agrees with its noun (here आत्मा, masculine singular, hence -व्यः).

(C) विभक्तिः in the texts: वित्तेन ('by wealth') and विद्यया / अविद्यया ('by knowledge') are तृतीया (instrumental — the means); मृत्योः, तमसः, असतः ('from death/darkness/the unreal') are पञ्चमी (ablative — the source moved away from); अमृतस्य ('of the immortal') is षष्ठी (genitive); अयनाय ('for going') is चतुर्थी (dative — purpose); मुक्तिं प्रति गति-अर्थे द्वितीया — सत्, ज्योतिः, अमृतम् are द्वितीया as goals of गमय ('lead TO the real, TO light, TO immortality').

(D) लोट्-लकारः (imperative): गमय ('lead!' — causative of गम्, 2nd person singular), शृण्वन्तु ('let them listen' — श्रु, 3rd person plural), एहि ('come!' — आ + इ), ब्रूहि ('tell!' — ब्रू). Compare विधिलिङ् forms in the dialogue: स्यात् / स्याम् ('would be / would I be'), कुर्याम् ('shall/should I do').

सारांश (SUMMARY)

अमृतस्य पन्थाः — the path of immortality — is the Upanishadic teaching that while everything material perishes, the आत्मा is deathless, and knowing it is the only way beyond the fear of death. The chapter's centre is the Brihadaranyaka dialogue in which Maitreyi, offered wealth by Yajnavalkya, asks whether it can make her immortal, and on hearing 'अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन' replies: येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम् — 'what shall I do with that by which I cannot become immortal?' Yajnavalkya then teaches: आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यः मन्तव्यः निदिध्यासितव्यः — the Self must be realized through hearing, reflection and deep meditation. Five mantras deepen the theme: असतो मा सद्गमय (lead me from death to immortality), शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः (all humans are children of immortality), विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते (by knowledge one attains immortality), श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च (the wise choose the good over the pleasant), and नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय (there is no other path). Grammar drawn from these texts covered सन्धि-विच्छेद, the तव्यत् gerundive, विभक्ति usage, and लोट् imperatives. The abiding lesson: wealth serves life; knowledge serves immortality — choose, like Maitreyi, the श्रेयस्.

topics.name: अमृतत्वम् — The Upanishadic Idea of Immortality
topics.description: The meaning of अमृतम् (अ + मृतम्, 'the deathless') and पन्थाः ('path'); immortality as realization of the imperishable आत्मा, not endless bodily life; the contrast of नित्य (eternal — आत्मा, विद्या) with अनित्य (transient — वित्तम्, शरीरम्, भोगाः).

topics.name: मैत्रेयी-याज्ञवल्क्य-संवादः — The Dialogue on Wealth and Immortality
topics.description: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad dialogue: Yajnavalkya's decision to renounce and divide his wealth, Maitreyi's question whether wealth can make her immortal, the reply 'अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन', and her famous words 'येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्'.

topics.name: आत्मविद्या — The Path of Self-Knowledge
topics.description: Yajnavalkya's teaching 'आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यः मन्तव्यः निदिध्यासितव्यः' — the discipline of श्रवणम् (hearing), मननम् (reflection) and निदिध्यासनम् (deep meditation) leading to दर्शनम् (realization); 'आत्मनस्तु कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति'.

topics.name: अमृत-मन्त्राः — Verses on Immortality with अन्वय
topics.description: Five public-domain Upanishadic texts with शब्दार्थ, अन्वय and translation: असतो मा सद्गमय (Brihadaranyaka), शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः and वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम् (Shvetashvatara), विद्यां चाविद्यां च (Isha), श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च (Katha).

topics.name: श्रेयः-प्रेयः-विवेकः — The Good versus the Pleasant
topics.description: The Katha Upanishad's distinction between श्रेयस् (the ultimately good) and प्रेयस् (the immediately pleasant); the धीरः who discriminates and chooses the good versus the मन्दः who chooses comfort; Maitreyi's choice as the model, and applications to modern student life.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Texts
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the chapter's sentences and mantras: सन्धि-विच्छेद (नामृता, मृत्योर्मा, सद्गमय, विद्ययाऽमृतम्, वेदाहम्), the तव्यत् gerundive (द्रष्टव्यः, श्रोतव्यः, मन्तव्यः, निदिध्यासितव्यः), विभक्ति usage (वित्तेन, मृत्योः, अमृतस्य, अयनाय), and लोट् imperatives (गमय, शृण्वन्तु, एहि, ब्रूहि).
