chapter_summary.title: अमृतस्य पन्थाः (Amritasya Panthah) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary covers Chapter 14 — the path of immortality. It presents the Upanishadic meaning of अमृतत्व, the Maitreyi–Yajnavalkya dialogue on wealth versus Self-knowledge, five key mantras with their meanings, the श्रेयः-प्रेयः discrimination, and grammar drawn from the texts.

branches.label: मैत्रेयी-संवादः — The dialogue
details: Yajnavalkya offers to divide his wealth
Maitreyi: can wealth make me immortal?
येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्

branches.label: श्रेयः-प्रेयः & व्याकरणम्
details: धीरः chooses श्रेयस्, मन्दः chooses प्रेयस्
सन्धि: नामृता = न + अमृता; मृत्योर्मा = मृत्योः + मा

sections.heading: The Upanishadic idea of immortality
bullets: अमृतम् is formed of the negative prefix अ + मृतम् (root मृ 'to die') — 'that which does not die'; पन्थाः means path, so the title means 'the path of immortality'.
The Upanishads (वेदान्त) do not promise that the body lives forever; the body is अनित्य. Immortality means realizing that the आत्मा is unborn and imperishable.
The chapter repeatedly contrasts the नित्य (आत्मा, विद्या, सत्यम्) with the अनित्य (वित्तम्, शरीरम्, भोगाः); the path is the turning from the second to the first.
तमेव विदित्वाति मृत्युमेति — 'knowing Him alone one crosses death' — states that Self-knowledge alone carries one beyond death, नान्यः पन्थाः, there is no other path.

sections.heading: The Maitreyi–Yajnavalkya dialogue
bullets: Yajnavalkya, about to renounce the householder's life, offered to divide his wealth between his wives Maitreyi and Katyayani; Maitreyi was a ब्रह्मवादिनी.
Maitreyi asked: if the whole earth full of wealth were mine, would I be immortal by it? Yajnavalkya answered that her life would merely be like that of the wealthy — अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन.
Maitreyi's reply — येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम् — 'what shall I do with that by which I cannot become immortal?' — is the chapter's central sentence.
Pleased, Yajnavalkya taught her the means of immortality: knowledge of the आत्मा, for whose sake alone all things — spouse, children, wealth — are dear (आत्मनस्तु कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति).

sections.heading: The path of Self-knowledge
bullets: आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यः मन्तव्यः निदिध्यासितव्यः — the Self must be seen; for that it must be heard about, reflected upon, and deeply meditated upon.

The threefold discipline is श्रवणम् (hearing the truth from teacher and Upanishad), मननम् (reasoning until doubts dissolve), निदिध्यासनम् (sustained deep meditation), culminating in दर्शनम् (direct realization).
When the Self is known, all this is known — the one thread on which every experience is strung.
The four words of the teaching are all तव्यत् gerundives, expressing what MUST be done — the Upanishad states the path as a duty, not a suggestion.

sections.heading: Mantras of immortality
bullets: असतो मा सद्गमय। तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय। मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय॥ (बृहदारण्यक) — lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to immortality.
शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः (श्वेताश्वतर) — all human beings are addressed as 'children of the Immortal'; deathlessness is our birthright.
विद्यां चाविद्यां च... विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते (ईश) — by worldly knowledge one crosses mortal needs; by Self-knowledge one attains immortality; both are honoured in their places.
श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च... (कठ) — the wise one (धीरः) examines the good and the pleasant and chooses the good; the dull one (मन्दः) chooses the pleasant for comfort's sake.
वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम्... नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय (श्वेताश्वतर) — knowing the sun-radiant Purusha beyond darkness is the ONLY path beyond death — the verse behind the chapter's title.

sections.heading: Grammar from the texts
bullets: सन्धि-विच्छेद: नामृता = न + अमृता; वेदाहम् = वेद + अहम् (दीर्घ); मृत्योर्मा = मृत्योः + मा and श्रेयश्च = श्रेयः + च (विसर्ग); सद्गमय = सत् + गमय (व्यञ्जन).
विद्ययाऽमृतम् = विद्यया + अमृतम् — the अवग्रह (ऽ) marks the merged अ.
तव्यत्-प्रत्यय (gerundive 'must be'): द्रष्टव्यः (दृश्), श्रोतव्यः (श्रु), मन्तव्यः (मन्), निदिध्यासितव्यः (नि+ध्यै).
विभक्ति: वित्तेन / विद्यया = तृतीया (means); मृत्योः, तमसः, असतः = पञ्चमी (from); अमृतस्य = षष्ठी; अयनाय = चतुर्थी (purpose).
लोट् imperatives: गमय (lead!), शृण्वन्तु (let them listen), एहि (come!), ब्रूहि (tell!); विधिलिङ्: स्याम्, कुर्याम्.

key_takeaways: अमृतस्य पन्थाः means 'the path of immortality' — the Upanishadic way beyond the fear of death through knowledge of the आत्मा.
Wealth can give comfort, never deathlessness: अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन.
Maitreyi's question — येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम् — models the seeker's discrimination between the eternal and the transient.
The path is आत्मविद्या through श्रवणम्, मननम् and निदिध्यासनम्: आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः.
विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते — by knowledge one attains immortality; worldly knowledge (अविद्या) and Self-knowledge (विद्या) each have their proper place.
The धीरः chooses श्रेयस् (the good) over प्रेयस् (the pleasant); every day offers this choice, and the path of immortality is walked through it.
Grammar from the texts: सन्धि-विच्छेद (नामृता = न + अमृता), तव्यत् gerundives (द्रष्टव्यः), विभक्ति of means and source (वित्तेन, मृत्योः), and लोट् imperatives (गमय, शृण्वन्तु).

glossary.definition: The deathless, the imperishable (अ + मृतम् from root मृ 'to die'); in the Upanishads, the state of immortality attained through knowledge of the Self.
Path or way; in the chapter title, the path that leads to immortality — नान्यः पन्थाः, there is no other path.
Wealth, property, riches; that which Yajnavalkya offered to divide and which, he taught, can never give immortality.
The innermost Self — unborn, undying and imperishable; that which must be seen, heard about, reflected on and meditated upon.
A woman devoted to the inquiry into Brahman; the epithet of Maitreyi, who preferred the knowledge of immortality to wealth.
Hearing the truth of the Self from the teacher and the Upanishads — the first step of the discipline of Self-knowledge.
Reflection — reasoning upon the heard truth until intellectual doubts are removed; the second step of the discipline.
Deep, sustained meditation on the truth of the Self; the third step, ripening into direct realization (दर्शनम्).
The ultimately good or beneficial, as opposed to the merely pleasant; what the wise person (धीरः) chooses (Katha Upanishad).
The immediately pleasant or agreeable; what the dull person (मन्दः) chooses for the sake of worldly comfort and security.
Knowledge — in this chapter especially the knowledge of the Self, by which one attains immortality: विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते.
In the Isha verse, knowledge of the world and of action, by which one crosses mortal needs — honoured together with विद्या, each in its place.
The wise, steadfast person who examines the good and the pleasant, discriminates between them, and chooses the good.
The gerundive suffix expressing 'must be / should be done', seen in द्रष्टव्यः, श्रोतव्यः, मन्तव्यः, निदिध्यासितव्यः.
The prose word-order of a verse — rearranging the words of a श्लोक or मन्त्र into natural sentence order to bring out its meaning.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — अमृतस्य पन्थाः (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 14)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give explanations in English. Quote the mantras and dialogue lines from the lesson wherever asked.

questions.question: 'विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते' — this famous line occurs in which Upanishad?
questions.answer: ईशोपनिषद्
questions.explanation: The verse विद्यां चाविद्यां च... अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते is from the Isha Upanishad.

questions.question: Besides Maitreyi, who was Yajnavalkya's other wife?
questions.answer: कात्यायनी
questions.explanation: Yajnavalkya had two wives — Maitreyi, the ब्रह्मवादिनी, and Katyayani.

questions.question: According to Yajnavalkya, there is no hope of immortality through wealth (अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन).
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: This is Yajnavalkya's exact teaching in the dialogue: wealth gives a comfortable life, but of immortality there is no hope through wealth.

questions.question: Complete the mantra: मृत्योर्मा ______ गमय।
questions.answer: अमृतम्
questions.explanation: The third line of the Pavamana mantra is मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय — 'lead me from death to immortality'.

questions.question: 'नामृता' इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः: न + ______।
questions.answer: अमृता
questions.explanation: नामृता = न + अमृता — दीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + अ = आ), as in येनाहं नामृता स्याम्.

questions.question: Give the meanings of the three words: श्रोतव्यः, मन्तव्यः, निदिध्यासितव्यः.
questions.answer: श्रोतव्यः = (the Self) must be heard about — श्रवणम्, hearing the truth from the teacher and the Upanishads; मन्तव्यः = must be reflected upon — मननम्, reasoning until doubts are removed; निदिध्यासितव्यः = must be deeply meditated upon — निदिध्यासनम्, sustained meditation ripening into realization.
questions.explanation: The three तव्यत् forms name the three steps of the discipline of आत्मविद्या in Yajnavalkya's teaching.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय and English translation of: विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह। अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते॥
questions.answer: अन्वयः: यः विद्यां च अविद्यां च — तत् उभयं सह वेद, (सः) अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्यया अमृतम् अश्नुते। Translation: One who knows both vidya (Self-knowledge) and avidya (worldly knowledge/action) together, crosses death by avidya and attains immortality by vidya.
questions.explanation: The Isha Upanishad honours both kinds of knowledge: worldly knowledge carries us across mortal needs; Self-knowledge alone gives immortality.

questions.question: Distinguish श्रेयस् from प्रेयस् as taught in the Katha Upanishad, with one example of each from student life.
questions.answer: श्रेयस् is the ultimately good or beneficial — what truly helps in the long run (e.g. steady daily study, healthy habits). प्रेयस् is the immediately pleasant — what feels good now (e.g. endless entertainment or scrolling instead of studying). The धीरः (wise one) examines both and chooses श्रेयस्; the मन्दः (dull one) chooses प्रेयस् for the sake of comfort (योगक्षेमात्).
questions.explanation: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः — the wise separates the two and chooses the good.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer: याज्ञवल्क्यः अवदत् — 'यथा उपकरणवतां जीवितं भवति, तथा एव तव जीवितं स्यात्। अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन' इति। (a) What, according to this reply, CAN wealth give Maitreyi? (b) What can it NOT give, and why? (c) What does this reveal about the difference between comfort and the highest goal?
questions.answer: (a) Wealth can give Maitreyi a life like that of people who possess every means and comfort (उपकरणवताम् इव जीवितम्) — ease, security, enjoyment. (b) It cannot give immortality (अमृतत्वम्), because wealth is external and perishable; it serves only the body and its needs, while immortality belongs to the realization of the imperishable आत्मा, which no external object can produce. (c) It reveals that comfort and the highest goal lie on different levels: comfort improves mortal life, but the highest goal — deathlessness — requires आत्मविद्या. Means of living cannot become the means of immortality.
questions.explanation: The reply separates the sphere of वित्तम् (comfortable living) from the sphere of विद्या (immortality) — the central analysis of the dialogue.

questions.question: Narrate the dialogue between Maitreyi and Yajnavalkya in your own words, quoting at least two key Sanskrit sentences, and state the message of the dialogue.
questions.answer: Model answer: The sage Yajnavalkya, wishing to renounce the householder's life, told his wife Maitreyi that he would divide his wealth between her and Katyayani. Maitreyi, a ब्रह्मवादिनी, asked whether the whole earth full of wealth could make her immortal. Yajnavalkya answered honestly: her life would be like the life of the wealthy, but 'अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन' — there is no hope of immortality through wealth. Maitreyi then spoke her famous sentence: 'येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्?' — 'What shall I do with that by which I cannot become immortal?' — and asked him to teach her instead what he knew. Pleased, Yajnavalkya taught: 'आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः' — the Self must be realized through hearing, reflection and deep meditation; all things are dear only for the sake of the Self, and by knowing it, all is known. Message: wealth serves mortal life only; the path of immortality is the knowledge of the Self, and the true seeker, like Maitreyi, chooses the eternal over the transient.
questions.explanation: Full marks require the narrative frame, two correct Sanskrit quotations, and a clear statement of the message.

questions.question: What is the literal meaning of the word अमृतम्?
options: That which does not die (the deathless)
questions.answer: That which does not die (the deathless)
questions.explanation: अमृतम् = अ (not) + मृतम् (dead, from root मृ 'to die') — the deathless, the imperishable.

questions.question: The chapter title 'अमृतस्य पन्थाः' means:
questions.answer: The path of immortality
questions.explanation: अमृतस्य (of immortality, षष्ठी) + पन्थाः (path) = the path of immortality.

questions.question: In the Upanishadic sense, अमृतत्वम् (immortality) chiefly means:
options: Realization that the आत्मा is imperishable
questions.answer: Realization that the आत्मा is imperishable
questions.explanation: The Upanishads do not promise endless bodily life; immortality is the knowledge that one's true Self is unborn and undying.

questions.question: Which of the following is नित्य (eternal) according to the chapter?
questions.answer: आत्मा
questions.explanation: The आत्मा alone is नित्य; wealth, body and house are all अनित्य (perishable).

questions.question: The word अमृत is derived from which Sanskrit root?
questions.answer: मृ (to die)
questions.explanation: मृ 'to die' gives मृतम् 'dead'; with the negative prefix अ, अमृतम् = the deathless.

questions.question: According to the chapter, which of these can NEVER be purchased by wealth?
questions.answer: अमृतत्वम्
questions.explanation: Wealth buys houses, food and clothing — the comforts of mortal life — but अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन: immortality cannot be bought.

questions.question: The Upanishads are called वेदान्त because they are:
options: The concluding, philosophical portions of the Vedas
The oldest hymns of the Vedas
questions.answer: The concluding, philosophical portions of the Vedas
questions.explanation: वेद + अन्त = 'the end of the Veda' — the Upanishads form the final, philosophical portion of Vedic literature.

questions.question: Which pair below is correctly matched?
questions.answer: वित्तम् — अनित्यम्; आत्मा — नित्यः
questions.explanation: Wealth is transient (अनित्य) while the Self is eternal (नित्य) — the chapter's basic contrast.

questions.question: What is the opposite (विलोम) of अमृतम् used in the chapter's texts?
questions.answer: मृत्युः
questions.explanation: मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय — 'from death (मृत्युः) lead me to immortality (अमृतम्)' — the two stand opposed.

questions.question: The dialogue between Maitreyi and Yajnavalkya is found in which Upanishad?
questions.answer: बृहदारण्यकोपनिषद्
questions.explanation: The celebrated Maitreyi–Yajnavalkya dialogue occurs in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.

questions.question: What did Yajnavalkya wish to do at the beginning of the dialogue?
options: Leave the householder's life and take up renunciation
questions.answer: Leave the householder's life and take up renunciation
questions.explanation: Yajnavalkya announced he was about to go forth (उद्यास्यन्) from the householder's state into संन्यास.

questions.question: Before leaving, what did Yajnavalkya offer to do for his wives?
options: Take them along on his journey
questions.answer: Divide his wealth between them
questions.explanation: He said: 'एहि, तव कात्यायन्याः च कृते वित्तस्य विभागं करोमि' — let me divide my wealth for you and Katyayani.

questions.question: Maitreyi is honoured in the tradition with which epithet?
questions.answer: ब्रह्मवादिनी
questions.explanation: Maitreyi is called ब्रह्मवादिनी — a woman devoted to the inquiry into Brahman.

questions.question: What was Maitreyi's first question to Yajnavalkya?
options: If the whole earth full of wealth were mine, would I become immortal by it?
Where will you go after renunciation?
Why do you not divide the wealth equally?
Who will teach me after you leave?
questions.answer: If the whole earth full of wealth were mine, would I become immortal by it?
questions.explanation: She asked: यदि इयं सर्वा पृथिवी वित्तेन पूर्णा मम स्यात्, किं तेन अहम् अमृता स्याम्?

questions.question: Complete Yajnavalkya's reply: 'अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति ______।'
questions.answer: वित्तेन
questions.explanation: अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन — 'of immortality there is no hope through wealth'.

questions.question: 'येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्' — who speaks this sentence?
questions.answer: मैत्रेयी
questions.explanation: Maitreyi speaks the famous sentence: 'What shall I do with that by which I cannot become immortal?'

questions.question: Instead of wealth, what did Maitreyi ask Yajnavalkya to give her?
options: The knowledge of immortality that he possessed
His blessings for a long life
questions.answer: The knowledge of immortality that he possessed
questions.explanation: She said: यत् एव भगवान् वेद — अमृतत्वस्य साधनम् — तत् एव मे ब्रूहि ('tell me only that which you know — the means of immortality').

questions.question: According to Yajnavalkya, with abundant wealth Maitreyi's life would become like the life of:
options: People who possess every means and comfort (उपकरणवताम्)
questions.answer: People who possess every means and comfort (उपकरणवताम्)
questions.explanation: यथा उपकरणवतां जीवितं भवति, तथा एव तव जीवितं स्यात् — wealth gives the life of the well-provided, nothing more.

questions.question: Why, according to the chapter, can wealth NOT give immortality?
options: It is external and perishable, serving only the body's needs
It is forbidden to seekers by the scriptures
It always creates enemies and quarrels
It belongs to the king and not to individuals
questions.answer: It is external and perishable, serving only the body's needs
questions.explanation: Wealth is अनित्य and external; it can furnish comfort for mortal life but cannot touch the आत्मा, whose realization alone is immortality.

questions.question: Maitreyi's choice of knowledge over wealth chiefly demonstrates which quality?
options: विवेकः (discrimination between the eternal and the transient)
questions.answer: विवेकः (discrimination between the eternal and the transient)
questions.explanation: She measures wealth against the highest goal and finds it insufficient — the classic act of विवेक, discrimination.

questions.question: The rhetorical force of 'किमहं तेन कुर्याम्' ('what shall I do with that?') expresses:
options: Rejection of whatever cannot serve the highest goal
Anger at being offered too little
A request for more time to decide
questions.answer: Rejection of whatever cannot serve the highest goal
questions.explanation: The question dismisses wealth not with contempt but because it fails the one test that matters to her — immortality.

questions.question: The Maitreyi–Yajnavalkya dialogue is fundamentally a contrast between:
options: Northern and southern recensions of the Veda
questions.answer: वित्तम् (wealth) and आत्मविद्या (Self-knowledge)
questions.explanation: The whole dialogue turns on the opposition between perishable wealth and the knowledge of the imperishable Self.

questions.question: Why was Yajnavalkya pleased with Maitreyi's response?
options: Because she preferred the eternal truth to material inheritance
Because she agreed to accept the division of wealth
Because she promised to accompany him
Because she recited the Vedas correctly
questions.answer: Because she preferred the eternal truth to material inheritance
questions.explanation: He said she was dear to him and spoke what was dear — her question proved she was a true seeker of the eternal.

questions.question: Which modern statement best parallels Yajnavalkya's teaching on wealth?
options: Money can buy comfort, but not meaning or fearlessness
Money is the root of all progress
Wealth should be renounced by every student
Comfort and immortality are the same pursuit
questions.answer: Money can buy comfort, but not meaning or fearlessness
questions.explanation: The dialogue's point survives translation to today: wealth furnishes the means of living, not the answer to death.

questions.question: The central question of the dialogue can best be restated as:
options: Can the means of mortal life ever produce immortality?
Should property be divided equally among heirs?
Is renunciation superior to household life?
Which of the two wives deserved more wealth?
questions.answer: Can the means of mortal life ever produce immortality?
questions.explanation: Maitreyi's question probes whether anything belonging to mortal life — wealth above all — can yield the deathless.

questions.question: Maitreyi did not despise wealth; she rejected it because:
options: It failed the test of the highest goal she had set
The scriptures forbid women to own property
She feared the burden of protecting it
questions.answer: It failed the test of the highest goal she had set
questions.explanation: Her rejection is an act of measurement, not contempt: wealth is good for living, useless for immortality.

questions.question: For a student today, the dialogue's most direct lesson is:
options: Pursue lasting knowledge and character, not only material gain
Refuse all family property on principle
Avoid earning money in adult life
Postpone education until wealth is secured
questions.answer: Pursue lasting knowledge and character, not only material gain
questions.explanation: The dialogue does not condemn earning; it teaches that the enduring goods — knowledge, truth, self-realization — must rank first.

questions.question: 'आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः' — how many disciplines toward realization does this sentence name after 'द्रष्टव्यः'?
questions.answer: Three — श्रवणम्, मननम्, निदिध्यासनम्
questions.explanation: The Self is to be SEEN (goal); the three means named are hearing (श्रोतव्यः), reflection (मन्तव्यः) and deep meditation (निदिध्यासितव्यः).

questions.question: श्रोतव्यः means the Self:
options: Must be heard about (from teacher and scripture)
questions.answer: Must be heard about (from teacher and scripture)
questions.explanation: श्रु + तव्यत् = 'must be heard' — श्रवणम्, receiving the truth of the Self from the guru and the Upanishads.

questions.question: मननम्, the second step of the discipline, means:
options: Reasoning upon the heard truth until doubts are removed
questions.answer: Reasoning upon the heard truth until doubts are removed
questions.explanation: मननम् is reflection — turning the heard teaching over in the reason until intellectual doubt dissolves.

questions.question: निदिध्यासनम् is best described as:
options: Deep, sustained meditation on the truth of the Self
questions.answer: Deep, sustained meditation on the truth of the Self
questions.explanation: निदिध्यासनम् is the profound, continuous meditation that ripens hearing and reflection into direct realization.

questions.question: 'आत्मनस्तु कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति' teaches that:
options: All things are dear for the sake of the Self
One should love only oneself and no other
Only family members deserve our love
questions.answer: All things are dear for the sake of the Self
questions.explanation: Husband, wife, children, wealth — all are dear not in themselves but for the sake of the Self, the one supreme reality within.

questions.question: According to Yajnavalkya, what happens when the आत्मा is truly known?
questions.answer: All this becomes known
questions.explanation: आत्मनः दर्शनेन एव इदं सर्वं विदितं भवति — with the realization of the Self, everything is known, as all experience is strung on it.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the steps on the path of Self-knowledge?
questions.answer: श्रवणम् → मननम् → निदिध्यासनम् → दर्शनम्
questions.explanation: First hear the truth, then reflect on it, then meditate deeply — and realization (दर्शनम्) is the culmination.

questions.question: In Yajnavalkya's teaching, from whom or what is the truth of the Self first to be heard (श्रवणम्)?
options: From the teacher and the Upanishads
questions.answer: From the teacher and the Upanishads
questions.explanation: श्रवणम् means receiving the teaching from the guru and the scripture — the authoritative sources of आत्मविद्या.

questions.question: In the sentence 'आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः...', the word आत्मा refers to:
options: The innermost Self, distinct from body and mind
questions.answer: The innermost Self, distinct from body and mind
questions.explanation: आत्मा here is the imperishable inner Self — not the body, senses or mind, which are its instruments.

questions.question: Yajnavalkya declares that immortality is attained by:
questions.answer: आत्मज्ञानेन (knowledge of the Self) alone
questions.explanation: न वित्तेन, न कर्मणा, किन्तु आत्मज्ञानेन एव अमृतत्वं लभ्यते — not by wealth or acts, but by Self-knowledge alone.

questions.question: What is the third line of the mantra beginning 'असतो मा सद्गमय'?
questions.answer: मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय
questions.explanation: असतो मा सद्गमय। तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय। मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय॥ — the third line asks to be led from death to immortality.

questions.question: The mantra 'असतो मा सद्गमय...' occurs in which Upanishad?
questions.answer: बृहदारण्यकोपनिषद्
questions.explanation: This prayer (the Pavamana mantra) occurs in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.

questions.question: 'शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः' — this call occurs in which Upanishad?
questions.answer: श्वेताश्वतरोपनिषद्
questions.explanation: The Shvetashvatara Upanishad addresses all beings: 'Listen, all ye children of the Immortal!'

questions.question: The verse 'श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः...' belongs to which Upanishad?
questions.answer: कठोपनिषद्
questions.explanation: The teaching on श्रेयस् and प्रेयस् is given in the Katha Upanishad.

questions.question: In 'वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम्...', the great Purusha is described as:
options: Seated in the middle of the ocean
questions.answer: आदित्यवर्ण (sun-radiant) and beyond darkness
questions.explanation: आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् — radiant like the sun, beyond all darkness.

questions.question: 'तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय' is a prayer to be led from darkness to:
questions.answer: Light
questions.explanation: तमसः = from darkness; ज्योतिः = to light — the second movement of the Pavamana mantra.

questions.question: Whom does the phrase 'अमृतस्य पुत्राः' address?
options: All human beings as children of the Immortal
Only the sons of the sages
questions.answer: All human beings as children of the Immortal
questions.explanation: The Upanishad calls every human being a child of immortality — deathlessness is the birthright of all.

questions.question: Complete the line: 'अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा ______।'
questions.answer: विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते
questions.explanation: The Isha verse ends: विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते — 'by knowledge one attains immortality'.

questions.question: 'नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय' asserts that:
options: There exists no other path for that journey
Many paths lead to the same goal
The path is closed to householders
The path was lost long ago
questions.answer: There exists no other path for that journey
questions.explanation: न अन्यः पन्थाः विद्यते अयनाय — knowing the supreme Purusha is the ONLY way beyond death.

questions.question: Which mantra of the chapter directly gives it its title-idea of a 'path' (पन्थाः)?
options: वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम्... नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय
questions.answer: वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम्... नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय
questions.explanation: The word पन्थाः appears in this Shvetashvatara verse: knowledge of the Purusha is the one path — अमृतस्य पन्थाः.

questions.question: The word अश्नुते (in विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते) means:
questions.answer: Attains, obtains
questions.explanation: अश्नुते (from अश् 'to reach, pervade') here means 'attains' — by knowledge one attains immortality.

questions.question: तीर्त्वा (in अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा) means:
questions.answer: Having crossed
questions.explanation: तीर्त्वा is the gerund of तॄ 'to cross' — 'having crossed death (mortal difficulties) by avidya'.

questions.question: In 'असतो मा सद्गमय', the word सत् means:
questions.answer: The real, the true
questions.explanation: असत् = the unreal; सत् = the real/true being — 'lead me from the unreal to the real'.

questions.question: शृण्वन्तु means:
questions.answer: Let them listen
questions.explanation: शृण्वन्तु is लोट् (imperative), 3rd person plural of श्रु — 'let (all) listen!'

questions.question: परस्तात् (in तमसः परस्तात्) means:
questions.answer: Beyond
questions.explanation: तमसः परस्तात् = 'beyond darkness' — the Purusha is beyond all ignorance and gloom.

questions.question: Which is the correct अन्वय of 'विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह'?
options: यः विद्यां च अविद्यां च तत् उभयं सह वेद
विद्या च अविद्या च यं सह वेदयतः
यः उभयं विद्यया अविद्यया सह वदति
तत् उभयं यः विद्यायाः अविद्यायाः वेदः
questions.answer: यः विद्यां च अविद्यां च तत् उभयं सह वेद
questions.explanation: The prose order is: 'he who knows vidya and avidya — both together...' — यः विद्यां च अविद्यां च तत् उभयं सह वेद.

questions.question: वृणीते (in श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभिप्रेयसो वृणीते) means:
questions.answer: Chooses
questions.explanation: वृणीते (from वृ 'to choose') — the wise one CHOOSES the good over the pleasant.

questions.question: In the Katha verse, धीरः is best translated as:
questions.answer: The wise, steadfast person
questions.explanation: धीरः is the person of firm understanding who examines and discriminates — opposed to the मन्दः, the dull one.

questions.question: योगक्षेमात् (in प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते) refers to:
questions.answer: Worldly acquisition and security
questions.explanation: योग = acquiring what one lacks; क्षेम = keeping what one has. The dull one chooses the pleasant for the sake of worldly gain and safety.

questions.question: श्रेयस् means:
questions.answer: The ultimately good or beneficial
questions.explanation: श्रेयस् is the truly good — what benefits in the long run, even if it is not immediately pleasant.

questions.question: प्रेयस् means:
questions.answer: The immediately pleasant or agreeable
questions.explanation: प्रेयस् is what pleases at once — comfort, enjoyment — regardless of long-term benefit.

questions.question: According to the Katha Upanishad, who chooses श्रेयस्?
questions.answer: धीरः (the wise one)
questions.explanation: श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभिप्रेयसो वृणीते — the wise one chooses the good over the pleasant.

questions.question: According to the same verse, the मन्दः chooses प्रेयस् because of:
options: Concern for worldly gain and security (योगक्षेम)
questions.answer: Concern for worldly gain and security (योगक्षेम)
questions.explanation: प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते — the dull one chooses the pleasant for the sake of acquisition and safety.

questions.question: 'तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः' means the wise one:
options: Examines both well and discriminates between them
Abandons both the good and the pleasant
Asks others to choose for him
questions.answer: Examines both well and discriminates between them
questions.explanation: सम्परीत्य = having examined thoroughly; विविनक्ति = separates/discriminates — the wise one weighs both before choosing.

questions.question: In terms of the Katha verse, Maitreyi's choice in the dialogue was a choice of:
questions.answer: श्रेयस् over प्रेयस्
questions.explanation: She set aside pleasant, comfortable wealth (प्रेयस्) and chose the ultimately good — the knowledge of immortality (श्रेयस्).

questions.question: Which of the following is the best modern example of choosing श्रेयस्?
options: Steady daily study before an examination instead of late-night entertainment
Skipping meals to buy new gadgets
Watching one more episode because the day was tiring
Copying homework to save time for games
questions.answer: Steady daily study before an examination instead of late-night entertainment
questions.explanation: श्रेयस् is the long-term good; disciplined study over instant pleasure is the classic student-life instance.

questions.question: Repeatedly choosing प्रेयस् over श्रेयस्, the chapter implies, leads to:
options: Falling away from the higher goal of life
questions.answer: Falling away from the higher goal of life
questions.explanation: The pleasant, chosen for comfort's sake, gradually costs one the lasting good — the higher aim slips away.

questions.question: What is the सन्धि-विच्छेद of नामृता (in येनाहं नामृता स्याम्)?
questions.answer: न + अमृता
questions.explanation: न + अमृता = नामृता — दीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + अ = आ): 'by which I would NOT be immortal'.

questions.question: मृत्योर्मा is the sandhi form of:
questions.answer: मृत्योः + मा
questions.explanation: मृत्योः + मा → मृत्योर्मा — विसर्ग-सन्धि: the visarga becomes र् before the soft sound म्.

questions.question: What is the सन्धि-विच्छेद of सद्गमय?
questions.answer: सत् + गमय
questions.explanation: सत् + गमय → सद्गमय — व्यञ्जन-सन्धि: त् becomes द् before the soft consonant ग्.

questions.question: In विद्ययाऽमृतम्, the sign ऽ (अवग्रह) indicates:
options: An अ merged in sandhi (विद्यया + अमृतम्)
questions.answer: An अ merged in sandhi (विद्यया + अमृतम्)
questions.explanation: The avagraha marks the initial अ of अमृतम् that merged with the final आ of विद्यया.

questions.question: वेदाहम् (in वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम्) splits as:
questions.answer: वेद + अहम्
questions.explanation: वेद + अहम् → वेदाहम् — दीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + अ = आ): 'I know'.

questions.question: द्रष्टव्यः is formed with which suffix (प्रत्यय)?
questions.answer: तव्यत्
questions.explanation: दृश् + तव्यत् = द्रष्टव्यः — the gerundive, 'must be seen'.

questions.question: श्रोतव्यः is derived from which verbal root (धातु)?
questions.answer: श्रु
questions.explanation: श्रु 'to hear' + तव्यत् = श्रोतव्यः, 'must be heard'.

questions.question: गमय (in मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय) is which verb form?
options: लोट् (imperative) of the causative of गम् — 'lead!'
questions.answer: लोट् (imperative) of the causative of गम् — 'lead!'
questions.explanation: गमय is the imperative (लोट्) of the causative of गम् 'to go' — 'cause (me) to go, lead (me)'.

questions.question: In 'अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन', the word वित्तेन is in which विभक्ति?
questions.answer: तृतीया (instrumental)
questions.explanation: वित्तेन = 'by/through wealth' — the instrumental of means (तृतीया).

questions.question: In मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय, the word मृत्योः is in which विभक्ति?
questions.answer: पञ्चमी (ablative — 'from death')
questions.explanation: The prayer moves AWAY from death toward immortality; मृत्योः is पञ्चमी, the case of the source left behind.

questions.question: In 'नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय', the word अयनाय is in which विभक्ति and sense?
questions.answer: चतुर्थी — purpose ('for going/the journey')
questions.explanation: अयनाय is dative (चतुर्थी) of अयनम् 'going, path' — 'for that journey there is no other path'.

questions.question: The Maitreyi–Yajnavalkya dialogue is found in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The dialogue on wealth and immortality occurs in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.

questions.question: Maitreyi gladly accepted her share when Yajnavalkya offered to divide his wealth.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: She declined the wealth, asking instead: 'येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्?' — she wanted the knowledge of immortality, not property.

questions.question: According to the chapter, immortality can be attained through great wealth.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: Yajnavalkya's teaching is the opposite: अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन — there is no hope of immortality through wealth.

questions.question: The sentence 'आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः...' prescribes श्रवणम्, मननम् and निदिध्यासनम् as the discipline of Self-knowledge.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: श्रोतव्यः, मन्तव्यः and निदिध्यासितव्यः name exactly these three steps, leading to दर्शनम् (realization).

questions.question: The call 'शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः' occurs in the Shvetashvatara Upanishad.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The Shvetashvatara Upanishad addresses all beings as children of the Immortal.

questions.question: The line 'विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते' is from the Katha Upanishad.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: It is from the Isha Upanishad (विद्यां चाविद्यां च...); the Katha Upanishad gives the श्रेयस्-प्रेयस् verse.

questions.question: According to the Katha Upanishad, the धीरः (wise one) chooses प्रेयस् (the pleasant).
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: The wise one chooses श्रेयस् (the good); it is the मन्दः (dull one) who chooses the pleasant.

questions.question: The सन्धि-विच्छेद of नामृता is न + अमृता.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: न + अमृता → नामृता by दीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + अ = आ).

questions.question: द्रष्टव्यः is a verb form of the लोट् लकार (imperative).
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: द्रष्टव्यः is not a finite imperative; it is a तव्यत् gerundive (दृश् + तव्यत्) meaning 'must be seen'.

questions.question: Yajnavalkya told Maitreyi that with wealth her life would be like that of the well-provided, but immortality would remain out of reach.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: यथा उपकरणवतां जीवितं भवति, तथा एव तव जीवितं स्यात्; अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन।

questions.question: Complete the mantra: मृत्योर्मा ______ गमय।
questions.answer: अमृतम्
questions.explanation: मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय — 'lead me from death to immortality'.

questions.question: Complete the mantra: असतो मा ______ गमय।
questions.answer: सत्
questions.explanation: असतो मा सद्गमय — 'lead me from the unreal to the real (सत्)'; सत् + गमय = सद्गमय.

questions.question: Complete the line: शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य ______।
questions.answer: पुत्राः
questions.explanation: शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः — 'Listen, all ye children of the Immortal!'

questions.question: Complete Yajnavalkya's teaching: आत्मा वा अरे ______ श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः।
questions.answer: द्रष्टव्यः
questions.explanation: आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः... — 'the Self, dear one, must be SEEN' — the goal that the other three disciplines serve.

questions.question: Complete Yajnavalkya's reply: अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति ______।
questions.answer: वित्तेन
questions.explanation: अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन — 'of immortality there is no hope through wealth'.

questions.question: Complete Maitreyi's sentence: येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं ______ कुर्याम्?
questions.answer: तेन
questions.explanation: येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम् — 'what shall I do with THAT (तेन) by which I cannot become immortal?'

questions.question: Complete the Isha verse (अन्वय order): अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्यया ______ अश्नुते।
questions.answer: अमृतम्
questions.explanation: विद्यया अमृतम् अश्नुते — 'by knowledge one attains immortality' (विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते).

questions.question: Complete the Katha line: श्रेयो हि ______ अभि प्रेयसो वृणीते।
questions.answer: धीरः
questions.explanation: श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभिप्रेयसो वृणीते — the WISE one (धीरः) chooses the good over the pleasant.

questions.question: Complete the Katha line: प्रेयो ______ योगक्षेमाद् वृणीते।
questions.answer: मन्दः
questions.explanation: प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते — the DULL one (मन्दः) chooses the pleasant for the sake of worldly gain and security.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं कुरुत: मृत्योर्मा = ______ + मा।
questions.answer: मृत्योः
questions.explanation: मृत्योः + मा → मृत्योर्मा — विसर्ग-सन्धि (visarga becomes र् before the soft म्).

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदं कुरुत: वेदाहम् = वेद + ______।
questions.answer: अहम्
questions.explanation: वेद + अहम् → वेदाहम् — दीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + अ = आ).

questions.question: द्रष्टव्यः, श्रोतव्यः, मन्तव्यः — एतेषु पदेषु ______ इति प्रत्ययः अस्ति।
questions.answer: तव्यत्
questions.explanation: All three are gerundives formed with the तव्यत् suffix, expressing 'must be / should be done'.

questions.question: यत् कदापि न म्रियते तत् ______ इति उच्यते। (One word from the chapter title.)
questions.answer: अमृतम्
questions.explanation: That which never dies is called अमृतम् — the deathless (अ + मृतम्).

questions.question: Complete the teaching: आत्मनस्तु कामाय सर्वं ______ भवति।
questions.answer: प्रियम्
questions.explanation: आत्मनस्तु कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति — 'for the sake of the Self everything becomes DEAR (प्रियम्)'.

questions.question: Complete the Shvetashvatara line: वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं ______ आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात्।
questions.answer: महान्तम्
questions.explanation: वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम् — 'I know this GREAT Purusha, sun-radiant, beyond darkness.'

questions.question: Explain the meaning of अमृतम् in the Upanishadic sense. How is it different from the body living forever?
questions.answer: अमृतम् (अ + मृतम्, from root मृ 'to die') means 'the deathless'. In the Upanishads it does not mean that the body will live forever — the body is अनित्य and must die. Immortality is the realization that one's true Self, the आत्मा, is unborn, undying and imperishable; one who knows this crosses beyond the fear of death.
questions.explanation: The distinction between bodily continuance and Self-realization is the chapter's foundational idea.

questions.question: Why is the chapter titled 'अमृतस्य पन्थाः'? Which verse most directly supplies this title-idea?
questions.answer: The title means 'the path of immortality' — the way by which a person rises beyond death, namely the knowledge of the imperishable Self. The Shvetashvatara verse 'वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम्... तमेव विदित्वाति मृत्युमेति नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय' supplies the idea directly: knowing the supreme Purusha is the ONE path (पन्थाः) beyond death — there is no other.
questions.explanation: The word पन्थाः itself occurs in the Shvetashvatara verse, tying the title to the text.

questions.question: Distinguish नित्य from अनित्य, giving two examples of each from the chapter.
questions.answer: नित्य means eternal, imperishable — what does not decay or die: e.g. the आत्मा (the Self) and विद्या/सत्यम् (knowledge of truth). अनित्य means transient, perishable — what arises and passes away: e.g. वित्तम् (wealth) and शरीरम् (the body). The path of immortality is the deliberate turning from the अनित्य to the नित्य.
questions.explanation: The नित्य–अनित्य contrast structures the entire chapter, from the dialogue to the mantras.

questions.question: Why did Yajnavalkya propose to divide his wealth, and between whom?
questions.answer: Yajnavalkya had resolved to leave the householder's life (गृहस्थाश्रम) and take up renunciation (संन्यास). Before going forth (उद्यास्यन्), he wished to settle his worldly affairs, so he proposed to divide his wealth between his two wives — Maitreyi and Katyayani.
questions.explanation: The offer of division sets the stage for Maitreyi's question about wealth and immortality.

questions.question: Write Maitreyi's famous question in Sanskrit and translate it into English.
questions.answer: Sanskrit: येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्? Translation: 'What shall I do with that by which I cannot become immortal?' She asked this after learning that even the whole earth full of wealth could not give her immortality, and requested instead the knowledge that Yajnavalkya possessed.
questions.explanation: This sentence is the heart of the chapter — the seeker's measure applied to all possessions.

questions.question: What was Yajnavalkya's first reply when Maitreyi asked whether wealth could make her immortal?
questions.answer: He said 'No' — her life would merely become like the life of people who possess every means and comfort (यथा उपकरणवतां जीवितं भवति, तथा एव तव जीवितं स्यात्), but of immortality there is no hope through wealth: अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन.
questions.explanation: The reply concedes wealth's real but limited power: comfort yes, deathlessness no.

questions.question: Why is Maitreyi called ब्रह्मवादिनी? Justify the epithet from her conduct in the dialogue.
questions.answer: ब्रह्मवादिनी means a woman devoted to the inquiry into Brahman, the ultimate reality. Maitreyi earns the title by her conduct: offered the whole of her husband's wealth, she measures it against the highest goal — immortality — and finding it useless for that end, she rejects it and asks instead for the knowledge of the Self. Her single-pointed concern with the eternal, not the comfortable, is exactly the mark of a ब्रह्मवादिनी.
questions.explanation: The epithet is justified by her question येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम् and her request for आत्मविद्या.

questions.question: Explain: 'Wealth gives a comfortable life but not immortality.' Why is this so, according to the chapter?
questions.answer: Wealth is external and perishable (अनित्य); its whole power lies in furnishing means (उपकरणम्) — food, shelter, comfort — for the body's mortal life. Immortality, however, is not a possession but the realization of the imperishable आत्मा within. Since no external, perishable object can produce knowledge of the imperishable, wealth can perfect only the quality of mortal living, never carry one beyond death: अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन.
questions.explanation: The argument turns on the category difference between external means and inner realization.

questions.question: What does Maitreyi's rejection of wealth teach a student of today? Give a concrete application.
questions.answer: It teaches ordering one's priorities by what endures: knowledge, truth and character outlast marks, gadgets and money. A student applies it by measuring choices against the long-term goal — e.g. choosing genuine understanding over shortcuts and copying, or investing time in learning and health rather than only in status and consumption. Like Maitreyi, one need not despise money; one must simply refuse to let it displace the higher aim.
questions.explanation: The lesson is proportion, not renunciation: the transient serves; the eternal leads.

questions.question: Explain the three disciplines श्रवणम्, मननम् and निदिध्यासनम्.
questions.answer: श्रवणम् is hearing the truth of the Self from the teacher and the Upanishads — receiving the teaching from authoritative sources. मननम् is reflection — reasoning upon the heard truth again and again until intellectual doubts are removed. निदिध्यासनम् is deep, sustained meditation upon that truth, ripening conviction into direct realization (दर्शनम्). Together they form the discipline prescribed in आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः.
questions.explanation: The three steps convert heard doctrine into examined conviction and finally into direct experience.

questions.question: Translate and briefly explain: आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः।
questions.answer: Translation: 'The Self, dear one, must be seen — must be heard about, must be reflected upon, must be deeply meditated upon.' Explanation: the goal is दर्शनम्, direct realization of the आत्मा; the three means are श्रवणम् (hearing from teacher and scripture), मननम् (reflection until doubt dissolves) and निदिध्यासनम् (profound meditation). The gerundive (तव्यत्) forms present the path as a necessity — what MUST be done by the seeker of immortality.
questions.explanation: This sentence from the Brihadaranyaka dialogue is the classical statement of the path of Self-knowledge.

questions.question: Explain the teaching 'आत्मनस्तु कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति' with one example.
questions.answer: The sentence means: 'It is for the sake of the Self that everything becomes dear.' Nothing is loved purely for its own sake — spouse, children, wealth, even learning are dear because they serve the one Self within, the deepest reality of the lover. Example: a mother loves her child most of all things, and the Upanishad points out that this love is finally rooted in the Self — remove the connection to one's own inmost being, and the dearness fades. Hence the Self is the supreme object of knowledge.
questions.explanation: The teaching redirects all love toward its true source — the आत्मा — making Self-knowledge the highest pursuit.

questions.question: Write the complete Pavamana mantra (असतो मा...) and give its meaning in English.
questions.answer: असतो मा सद्गमय। तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय। मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय॥ Meaning: 'Lead me from the unreal to the real; lead me from darkness to light; lead me from death to immortality.' It occurs in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, and its three movements are three descriptions of the single journey of Self-knowledge.
questions.explanation: The three petitions — सत्, ज्योतिः, अमृतम् — name the goal as reality, light and deathlessness.

questions.question: Name the source Upanishad of each: (a) शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः (b) विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते (c) श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः।
questions.answer: (a) श्वेताश्वतरोपनिषद् (Shvetashvatara Upanishad). (b) ईशोपनिषद् (Isha Upanishad — from the verse विद्यां चाविद्यां च...). (c) कठोपनिषद् (Katha Upanishad — the teaching on the good and the pleasant).
questions.explanation: Knowing the sources anchors each mantra in its Upanishad.

questions.question: Give the अन्वय and translation of: विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह। अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते॥
questions.answer: अन्वयः: यः विद्यां च अविद्यां च — तत् उभयं सह वेद, (सः) अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्यया अमृतम् अश्नुते। Translation: 'He who knows both vidya and avidya together crosses death by avidya and attains immortality by vidya.' Here अविद्या is worldly knowledge and action, which carries one across mortal needs, and विद्या is Self-knowledge, which alone gives immortality.
questions.explanation: The verse honours both kinds of knowledge, assigning each its proper sphere.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: अश्नुते, तीर्त्वा, वृणीते, धीरः, परस्तात्।
questions.answer: अश्नुते = attains, obtains; तीर्त्वा = having crossed; वृणीते = chooses; धीरः = the wise, steadfast person; परस्तात् = beyond. (E.g. विद्यया अमृतम् अश्नुते — by knowledge one ATTAINS immortality; तमसः परस्तात् — BEYOND darkness.)
questions.explanation: These five words are load-bearing vocabulary in the chapter's verses.

questions.question: Translate: तमेव विदित्वाति मृत्युमेति नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय।
questions.answer: 'Only by knowing Him (the great Purusha) does one cross beyond death; there exists no other path for that journey.' (तम् एव विदित्वा — knowing Him alone; अति मृत्युम् एति — one goes beyond death; न अन्यः पन्थाः विद्यते अयनाय — no other path exists for the going.)
questions.explanation: The Shvetashvatara line asserts the exclusiveness of the path of knowledge — the source of the chapter's title.

questions.question: State the difference between श्रेयस् and प्रेयस् with one example of each.
questions.answer: श्रेयस् is the ultimately good — what truly benefits in the long run even if hard now (e.g. regular exercise and steady study). प्रेयस् is the immediately pleasant — what gratifies now regardless of later cost (e.g. skipping study for continuous entertainment). The Katha Upanishad says both approach every person; the धीरः examines and chooses श्रेयस्, the मन्दः chooses प्रेयस् for comfort's sake.
questions.explanation: The distinction is between long-term good and short-term pleasure — the daily fork on the path of immortality.

questions.question: Why does the मन्दः (dull one) choose प्रेयस्, according to the Katha verse? Explain the word योगक्षेमात्.
questions.answer: The मन्दः chooses the pleasant योगक्षेमात् — 'for the sake of yoga-kshema', i.e. worldly acquisition (योग = obtaining what one lacks) and security (क्षेम = protecting what one has). Absorbed in getting and keeping comfort and possessions, he never pauses to examine what is ultimately good, and so drifts with immediate pleasure.
questions.explanation: योगक्षेम names the whole engine of worldly getting-and-keeping that drives the choice of प्रेयस्.

questions.question: Describe one situation from your own student life where the श्रेयस्-प्रेयस् choice appears, and state which choice the धीरः would make.
questions.answer: Model answer: On the evening before a test, the choice appears between revising thoroughly (श्रेयस्) and watching one more hour of videos (प्रेयस्). The धीरः, like Maitreyi measuring wealth against immortality, would examine both options, recognize that the pleasure is momentary and the learning lasting, and choose the revision — श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभिप्रेयसो वृणीते. (Any honest situation with the same structure earns full marks.)
questions.explanation: The question asks students to apply the Katha criterion to a real decision of their own.

questions.question: Perform सन्धि-विच्छेद: (a) नामृता (b) मृत्योर्मा (c) वेदाहम् (d) तमसो मा।
questions.answer: (a) नामृता = न + अमृता (दीर्घ-सन्धि, अ + अ = आ). (b) मृत्योर्मा = मृत्योः + मा (विसर्ग-सन्धि — visarga becomes र् before म्). (c) वेदाहम् = वेद + अहम् (दीर्घ-सन्धि). (d) तमसो मा = तमसः + मा (विसर्ग-सन्धि — visarga becomes ओ before the soft sound).
questions.explanation: All four forms come from the chapter's own sentences and mantras.

questions.question: What does the तव्यत् प्रत्यय express? Illustrate with two words from Yajnavalkya's teaching, naming their roots.
questions.answer: The तव्यत् suffix forms a gerundive expressing necessity or duty — 'must be / should be done'. From the teaching आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः...: द्रष्टव्यः = दृश् + तव्यत्, 'must be seen'; श्रोतव्यः = श्रु + तव्यत्, 'must be heard'. (Also मन्तव्यः from मन्, निदिध्यासितव्यः from नि + ध्यै.) The forms agree with आत्मा (masculine singular), hence the ending -व्यः.
questions.explanation: The gerundives turn the path of Self-knowledge into a stated duty of the seeker.

questions.question: Narrate the Maitreyi–Yajnavalkya dialogue of the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad in detail, quoting the key Sanskrit sentences, and bring out its central message.
questions.answer: Model answer: The sage Yajnavalkya, resolving to leave the householder's life for renunciation, said to his wife Maitreyi that he would divide his wealth between her and his other wife Katyayani. Maitreyi, a ब्रह्मवादिनी, asked: यदि इयं सर्वा पृथिवी वित्तेन पूर्णा मम स्यात्, किं तेन अहम् अमृता स्याम्? — if the whole earth full of wealth were hers, would she become immortal? Yajnavalkya answered honestly: her life would be like the life of the well-provided (उपकरणवताम् इव), but अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन — of immortality there is no hope through wealth. Maitreyi then uttered the sentence that has echoed ever since: येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्? — 'What shall I do with that by which I cannot become immortal?' — and begged him to teach her what he knew. Delighted — 'dear you are to me, and dear is what you speak' — Yajnavalkya taught the path: आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः — the Self must be realized through hearing, reflection and deep meditation; आत्मनस्तु कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति — all things are dear only for the sake of the Self; and when the Self is known, all is known. Central message: wealth equips mortal life but cannot cross death; the sole path of immortality is knowledge of the imperishable Self, and the true seeker chooses it as Maitreyi did.
questions.explanation: A full answer needs the narrative frame, at least two accurate quotations, the teaching, and the message.

questions.question: 'Wealth cannot buy immortality.' Analyse the argument of the dialogue in support of this statement and discuss its relevance in today's consumer culture.
questions.answer: Model answer: The dialogue's argument runs in three steps. First, wealth's real power is conceded — it furnishes उपकरणम्, the means of comfortable living; Yajnavalkya does not despise it. Second, its limit is exposed: wealth is external and perishable (अनित्य), so its effects reach only the body and its circumstances; it cannot produce the realization of the imperishable आत्मा, which alone is अमृतत्वम् — hence अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन. Third, Maitreyi draws the practical conclusion: whatever fails the test of the highest goal may be set aside — येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्. Relevance today: consumer culture implicitly promises that acquiring more will finally satisfy; yet possessions still leave the deepest questions — meaning, fear of loss and death — untouched. The dialogue teaches proportion: earn and use wealth for living, but seek what endures — knowledge, truth, self-realization — for life's ultimate aim. A society of Maitreyis would measure success not by accumulation but by wisdom and character.
questions.explanation: Marks for the three-step analysis, correct quotations, and a thoughtful application to the present day.

questions.question: Describe the path of Self-knowledge taught by Yajnavalkya — द्रष्टव्यः, श्रोतव्यः, मन्तव्यः, निदिध्यासितव्यः — explaining each stage and how the stages depend on one another.
questions.answer: Model answer: Yajnavalkya's sentence आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः sets one goal and three means. The goal is दर्शनम् (द्रष्टव्यः) — the Self must be SEEN, directly realized, not merely believed in. The first means is श्रवणम् (श्रोतव्यः): hearing the truth of the Self from the teacher and the Upanishads, since the subject is beyond the senses and must first be learnt from authority. The second is मननम् (मन्तव्यः): reflecting on the heard teaching with one's own reason until every doubt is examined and resolved — hearing without thinking remains borrowed knowledge. The third is निदिध्यासनम् (निदिध्यासितव्यः): deep, sustained meditation in which the reasoned conviction is dwelt upon until it becomes immediate experience. The stages depend on each other in strict order: without hearing there is nothing to reflect on; without reflection, meditation rests on unexamined belief; without meditation, reflection remains intellectual. Together they transform doctrine into realization — and with the Self known, says Yajnavalkya, all this is known, and all things are seen to be dear for the sake of the Self (आत्मनस्तु कामाय सर्वं प्रियं भवति).
questions.explanation: Full marks require all four terms, correct Sanskrit-to-stage mapping, and the logic of their sequence.

questions.question: Write any three mantras from this chapter with their source Upanishads, translations, and the message of each.
questions.answer: Model answer (any three suffice): (1) असतो मा सद्गमय। तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय। मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय॥ (बृहदारण्यकोपनिषद्) — 'Lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to immortality.' Message: the spiritual journey is one movement described three ways — toward reality, light and deathlessness. (2) शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः (श्वेताश्वतरोपनिषद्) — 'Listen, all ye children of the Immortal!' Message: every human being is a child of immortality; the highest knowledge is everyone's birthright. (3) विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह। अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते॥ (ईशोपनिषद्) — 'He who knows both vidya and avidya together crosses death by avidya and attains immortality by vidya.' Message: worldly knowledge and Self-knowledge are complementary; each has its sphere. (4) श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च... (कठोपनिषद्) — the wise one examines the good and the pleasant and chooses the good, while the dull one chooses the pleasant. Message: the path of immortality is walked through daily श्रेयस् choices. (5) वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तम्... नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय (श्वेताश्वतरोपनिषद्) — 'I know that great sun-radiant Purusha beyond darkness; knowing Him alone one crosses death; there is no other path.' Message: knowledge of the Supreme is THE path — the chapter's title-idea.
questions.explanation: Any three mantras with source, faithful translation and message earn full marks.

questions.question: Give the full Isha Upanishad verse विद्यां चाविद्यां च... with अन्वय, शब्दार्थ, translation, and an explanation of how विद्या and अविद्या work together.
questions.answer: Model answer: Verse: विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह। अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते॥ अन्वयः: यः विद्यां च अविद्यां च तत् उभयं सह वेद, (सः) अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्यया अमृतम् अश्नुते। शब्दार्थ: विद्या = knowledge of the Self; अविद्या = knowledge of the world and of action; उभयं सह = both together; वेद = knows; मृत्युं तीर्त्वा = having crossed death/mortal want; अमृतम् अश्नुते = attains immortality. Translation: 'He who knows both vidya and avidya together crosses death by avidya and attains immortality by vidya.' Explanation: the verse refuses to set worldly competence and spiritual wisdom against each other. By अविद्या — skills, work, science, right action — a person crosses the mortal difficulties of hunger, disease and disorder; but no amount of it touches deathlessness. By विद्या — knowledge of the imperishable Self — immortality is attained; but it does not by itself feed or heal the body. The complete human being cultivates both together (उभयं सह), letting worldly knowledge serve life and Self-knowledge crown it — a strikingly balanced charter for a student's education.
questions.explanation: Marks for verse, correct अन्वय, key शब्दार्थ, translation, and the complementarity argument.

questions.question: Discuss the Katha Upanishad's teaching on श्रेयस् and प्रेयस्, and evaluate how a senior-secondary student today should use this teaching in making decisions about studies, screen time and career.
questions.answer: Model answer: The Katha Upanishad teaches: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः। श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभिप्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते॥ Both the good (श्रेयस्) and the pleasant (प्रेयस्) approach every person in every significant choice. The wise one (धीरः) does three things: examines both (सम्परीत्य), separates them clearly (विविनक्ति), and chooses the good (वृणीते); the dull one (मन्दः) chooses the pleasant for the sake of getting and keeping comforts (योगक्षेमात्). Evaluation for a student today: (a) Studies — deep understanding is श्रेयस्; last-minute shortcuts and copying are प्रेयस्; the धीर chooses daily disciplined study. (b) Screen time — recreation has a place, but endless scrolling is प्रेयस् chosen from comfort; a fixed limit serving rest, not escape, is the discriminating course. (c) Career — choosing a path only for quick money or prestige is प्रेयस्-driven; weighing aptitude, service and long-term growth is श्रेयस्-driven. The verse does not demand joylessness — it demands examination before choice. Maitreyi is the model: she examined wealth against her highest goal and chose knowledge. A student who habitually asks 'is this my श्रेयस् or merely my प्रेयस्?' has already begun walking the path of immortality.
questions.explanation: Marks for the verse and its terms, the धीर/मन्द contrast, and a genuine evaluation across the three areas.

questions.question: Explain the Upanishadic concept of immortality (अमृतत्वम्). How does it differ from the everyday idea of not dying, and how do the texts of this chapter — the dialogue and the mantras — establish it?
questions.answer: Model answer: In everyday speech 'immortality' means the body never dying; the Upanishads teach something deeper. The body, being a product of matter, is अनित्य and must perish; no teaching can alter that. अमृतत्वम् is the direct realization that one's true identity is the आत्मा — unborn, undying, imperishable — so that death is seen to touch only the perishable sheath, not the Self. The chapter's texts establish this step by step. The dialogue removes the false candidate: wealth, the greatest worldly power, cannot give deathlessness — अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन — because an external, perishable thing cannot produce knowledge of the imperishable. It then names the true path: आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः — realization through hearing, reflection and meditation. The mantras confirm and universalize: मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय prays for the passage from death to deathlessness as a passage from unreality and darkness to reality and light — a change of knowledge, not of body; शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः declares every human a child of the Immortal; विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते states the means — knowledge; and तमेव विदित्वाति मृत्युमेति नान्यः पन्थाः declares its exclusiveness. Thus immortality is not endless duration of the mortal but awakening to the eternal already within — and its one path is विद्या.
questions.explanation: Marks for the concept, the body/Self distinction, and correct use of at least three texts as evidence.

questions.question: Write a grammar note on this chapter covering: (a) three सन्धि examples with their types, (b) the तव्यत् gerundive with all four forms from the dialogue, and (c) two लोट् (imperative) forms from the mantras with their meanings.
questions.answer: Model answer: (a) सन्धिः — (i) नामृता = न + अमृता and वेदाहम् = वेद + अहम् — दीर्घ-सन्धि, two similar simple vowels merging into one long vowel (अ + अ = आ); (ii) मृत्योर्मा = मृत्योः + मा — विसर्ग-सन्धि, the visarga becoming र् before the soft म् (likewise तमसो मा = तमसः + मा with visarga becoming ओ); (iii) सद्गमय = सत् + गमय — व्यञ्जन-सन्धि, the hard त् softening to द् before the voiced ग् (likewise तद्वेद = तत् + वेद). Also notable: विद्ययाऽमृतम् = विद्यया + अमृतम्, where the अवग्रह (ऽ) marks the merged अ. (b) तव्यत्-प्रत्ययः — the gerundive of necessity, 'must be done': द्रष्टव्यः (दृश्, 'must be seen'), श्रोतव्यः (श्रु, 'must be heard'), मन्तव्यः (मन्, 'must be reflected on'), निदिध्यासितव्यः (नि + ध्यै, 'must be deeply meditated upon'); all agree with आत्मा, masculine singular. (c) लोट्-लकारः — गमय ('lead!', imperative of the causative of गम्, in मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय) and शृण्वन्तु ('let them listen', 3rd person plural of श्रु, in शृण्वन्तु विश्वे अमृतस्य पुत्राः); the dialogue adds एहि ('come!') and ब्रूहि ('tell!').
questions.explanation: Marks for correct splits with type names, all four gerundives with roots, and two imperatives with parsing.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer the questions: याज्ञवल्क्यः महर्षिः गृहस्थाश्रमं परित्यज्य संन्यासं ग्रहीतुम् ऐच्छत्। सः मैत्रेयीम् उवाच — 'मैत्रेयि! अहम् अस्मात् स्थानात् उद्यास्यन् अस्मि। एहि, तव कात्यायन्याः च कृते वित्तस्य विभागं करोमि' इति। (a) What decision had Yajnavalkya taken? (b) What does उद्यास्यन् mean? (c) What did he propose to do before leaving, and for whom?
questions.answer: (a) Yajnavalkya had decided to leave the householder's life (गृहस्थाश्रम) and take up renunciation (संन्यास). (b) उद्यास्यन् means 'about to go forth / about to depart' — announcing his imminent renunciation. (c) Before leaving he proposed to divide his wealth (वित्तस्य विभागम्) between his two wives, Maitreyi and Katyayani, so that his worldly affairs would be settled.
questions.explanation: The passage is the opening frame of the Brihadaranyaka dialogue.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer the questions: मैत्रेयी अवदत् — 'येनाहं नामृता स्यां किमहं तेन कुर्याम्? यत् एव भगवान् वेद, तत् एव मे ब्रूहि' इति। (a) Who is the speaker and to whom does she speak? (b) Translate the first sentence. (c) What exactly does she ask for in place of wealth?
questions.answer: (a) The speaker is Maitreyi, addressing her husband, the sage Yajnavalkya. (b) 'What shall I do with that by which I cannot become immortal?' (c) She asks him to teach her only what he himself knows — the means of immortality, i.e. the knowledge of the Self (आत्मविद्या) — rather than giving her any share of wealth.
questions.explanation: The passage contains the chapter's most famous sentence and Maitreyi's counter-request.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer the questions: मैत्रेयी अपृच्छत् — 'यदि इयं सर्वा पृथिवी वित्तेन पूर्णा मम स्यात्, किं तेन अहम् अमृता स्याम्?' याज्ञवल्क्यः अवदत् — 'न इति। अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन' इति। (a) What hypothetical situation does Maitreyi propose? (b) Why does she frame the question so extremely? (c) What is the force of Yajnavalkya's blunt 'न इति'?
questions.answer: (a) She supposes the extreme case: the WHOLE earth, filled with wealth, belonging to her alone. (b) By taking wealth to its absolute maximum she eliminates the excuse that merely 'more wealth' might succeed — if even all the world's wealth fails, wealth as such is proven incapable. (c) The blunt 'No' concedes nothing to comforting illusion: however vast, wealth belongs to the perishable order and cannot produce the imperishable; hence अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन — no hope of immortality through wealth.
questions.explanation: The extreme hypothesis is a deliberate logical device: testing the limit case settles the general principle.

questions.question: Read the case and answer the questions: A successful businessman spends thirty years building enormous wealth. At sixty he confesses: 'I have everything money can buy, yet I fear old age and death exactly as I did when poor, and I do not know what my life has been for.' (a) Which sentence of Yajnavalkya does his confession illustrate? (b) Analyse his situation using the chapter's नित्य–अनित्य distinction. (c) What first step would the chapter prescribe for him?
questions.answer: (a) It illustrates अमृतत्वस्य तु नाशास्ति वित्तेन — wealth gave him the life of the well-provided (उपकरणवताम् इव) but no freedom from the fear of death. (b) He invested only in the अनित्य — money, status, possessions — all of which stop at the body and its circumstances; the नित्य — the आत्मा, knowledge, truth — he left unexplored, so his deepest need is unmet despite outer abundance. (c) The chapter would prescribe Maitreyi's turn: begin आत्मविद्या through श्रवणम् — hearing the truth of the Self from a teacher and the Upanishads — followed by मननम् and निदिध्यासनम्, redirecting life toward what endures.
questions.explanation: The modern case reproduces the dialogue's structure: maximum wealth, unchanged mortality.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer the questions: याज्ञवल्क्यः अवदत् — 'आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः। आत्मनः दर्शनेन एव इदं सर्वं विदितं भवति' इति। (a) Identify the four तव्यत् words and give their meanings. (b) Which of the four names the goal and which name the means? (c) What is promised as the result of आत्मदर्शन?
questions.answer: (a) द्रष्टव्यः = must be seen; श्रोतव्यः = must be heard about; मन्तव्यः = must be reflected upon; निदिध्यासितव्यः = must be deeply meditated upon. (b) द्रष्टव्यः names the goal — direct realization (दर्शनम्); the other three name the means: श्रवणम् (hearing), मननम् (reflection), निदिध्यासनम् (deep meditation). (c) The result promised: by the realization of the Self, all this becomes known (इदं सर्वं विदितं भवति) — knowing the one reality on which everything depends, everything is essentially known.
questions.explanation: The passage condenses the whole path of आत्मविद्या into one sentence of four gerundives.

questions.question: Read the mantra and answer the questions: असतो मा सद्गमय। तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय। मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय॥ (a) Name the source Upanishad. (b) List the three 'from → to' movements of the prayer. (c) Explain why the three petitions describe one single journey.
questions.answer: (a) बृहदारण्यकोपनिषद् (the Pavamana mantra). (b) From the unreal (असत्) to the real (सत्); from darkness (तमस्) to light (ज्योतिः); from death (मृत्युः) to immortality (अमृतम्). (c) They are three faces of one passage — ignorance of the Self is at once unreality (taking the passing for the permanent), darkness (absence of the light of knowledge) and death (identification with the mortal). The single remedy is आत्मविद्या: when knowledge dawns, the real is known, the darkness lifts, and deathlessness is realized — one journey described three ways.
questions.explanation: The mantra's three lines map exactly onto the chapter's theme of knowledge as the path of immortality.

questions.question: Read the verse and answer the questions: विद्यां चाविद्यां च यस्तद्वेदोभयं सह। अविद्यया मृत्युं तीर्त्वा विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते॥ (a) Give the meanings of तीर्त्वा and अश्नुते. (b) What is achieved by अविद्या and what by विद्या? (c) A student says: 'Spiritual knowledge alone matters; worldly studies are useless.' Answer him using this verse.
questions.answer: (a) तीर्त्वा = 'having crossed'; अश्नुते = 'attains'. (b) By अविद्या — knowledge of the world and of action — one crosses मृत्यु, the realm of mortal wants and difficulties; by विद्या — knowledge of the Self — one attains अमृतम्, immortality. (c) The verse itself refutes him: it praises the one who knows BOTH together (उभयं सह). Worldly studies are not useless — they are the appointed means of crossing life's mortal needs (food, health, livelihood); what they cannot do is confer immortality, which is विद्या's work. The complete student honours both, each in its own sphere.
questions.explanation: The verse's balance — उभयं सह — answers both the materialist and the anti-worldly extremes.

questions.question: Read the verse and answer the questions: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतः तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः। श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभिप्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते॥ (a) What do श्रेयस् and प्रेयस् mean? (b) How do the धीरः and the मन्दः differ in their manner of choosing? (c) Relate this verse to Maitreyi's decision in the dialogue.
questions.answer: (a) श्रेयस् = the ultimately good/beneficial; प्रेयस् = the immediately pleasant/agreeable. (b) The धीरः first examines both thoroughly (सम्परीत्य) and separates them (विविनक्ति), then chooses the good; the मन्दः does not examine at all — he drifts to the pleasant for the sake of worldly getting and keeping (योगक्षेमात्). The difference is not only in WHAT is chosen but in HOW: examination versus impulse. (c) Maitreyi enacted this verse: offered pleasant, comfortable wealth (प्रेयस्), she examined it against the highest goal, found it powerless for immortality, and chose the knowledge of the Self (श्रेयस्) — the very model of the धीरा.
questions.explanation: The Katha verse gives the general law of which Maitreyi's choice is the classic instance.

questions.question: Read the case and answer the questions: Two months before the board examination, Arjun receives a new gaming console as a gift. Each evening he must decide between two hours of revision and two hours of gaming. He reasons: 'Gaming relaxes me NOW; results come later, if at all.' (a) Identify the श्रेयस् and the प्रेयस् in Arjun's situation. (b) Evaluate his reasoning using the Katha verse's terms धीरः, मन्दः and योगक्षेमात्. (c) Suggest a wise resolution that honours both relaxation and the goal.
questions.answer: (a) श्रेयस्: steady revision securing his learning and future; प्रेयस्: immediate pleasure of gaming. (b) His reasoning is the मन्द pattern: he chooses by immediate comfort (योगक्षेमात् — the pull of present ease and enjoyment) without सम्परीक्षा, the examination the धीरः performs. Discounting the future ('later, if at all') is precisely how the pleasant defeats the good. A धीर would weigh the lasting value of each hour and choose revision. (c) A wise resolution discriminates rather than merely renounces: fixed revision hours first, a limited, scheduled slot of gaming as genuine rest afterwards — pleasure subordinated to the goal, as अविद्या is honoured under विद्या in the chapter.
questions.explanation: The case transfers the श्रेयस्-प्रेयस् analysis to a concrete student decision, rewarding evaluation over moralizing.

questions.question: Read the lines and answer the grammar questions: (i) मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय (ii) आत्मा वा अरे द्रष्टव्यः श्रोतव्यो मन्तव्यो निदिध्यासितव्यः (iii) विद्ययाऽमृतमश्नुते। (a) Perform सन्धि-विच्छेद of मृत्योर्मा and विद्ययाऽमृतम्. (b) In line (i), state the विभक्ति of मृत्योः and of अमृतम्, with reasons. (c) In line (ii), name the प्रत्यय shared by the four adjectival words and state what it expresses.
questions.answer: (a) मृत्योर्मा = मृत्योः + मा (विसर्ग-सन्धि — visarga becomes र् before the soft म्); विद्ययाऽमृतम् = विद्यया + अमृतम् (the final आ and initial अ merge; the अवग्रह ऽ marks the elided अ). (b) मृत्योः is पञ्चमी (ablative) — the source moved AWAY from ('from death'); अमृतम् is द्वितीया (accusative) — the goal of the motion verb गमय ('lead TO immortality'). (c) The shared suffix is तव्यत्, forming gerundives that express necessity or obligation — 'must be seen, must be heard about, must be reflected upon, must be deeply meditated upon'.
questions.explanation: One case question integrating the chapter's सन्धि, विभक्ति and कृदन्त teaching from the actual mantra lines.
